evidence: A dry run of patch.diff with `patch -p1 --dry-run` against a scratch copy of the base snapshot succeeded for CHANGELOG.md, rich/_windows_renderer.py, rich/console.py, rich/control.py, rich/segment.py, tests/test_console.py, tests/test_control.py and tests/test_windows_renderer.py (exit 0).
checks.json: patch_applies=true, commands=[], candidate_test_changes lists the three test files.

patch.diff only adds code and tests (for example the new test_set_window_title at tests/test_console.py:299-309); it removes no existing tests. Reference-only changes in tests/test_live.py and the reference's __main__ demo are absent from the candidate, which is not a deletion.
Renderer dispatch is in rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56, the same module as reference.diff:34-36.
Console method is in rich/console.py:1154-1169, next to set_alt_screen/show_cursor, the same place as the reference method (reference.diff:45-75).

Title control formatter is in rich/control.py:33 and the classmethod is in rich/control.py:151-161; the enum member is in rich/segment.py:52 and ControlCode is in rich/segment.py:55-60. These match the reference modules (reference.diff:95, 103-110, 136, 139-144).
Console.set_window_title(self, title: str) -> bool at rich/console.py:1154 matches reference.diff:45.
Control.title(cls, title: str) -> "Control" at rich/control.py:152 matches reference.diff:104.
Return semantics match: True only after self.control(Control.title(title)) when is_terminal (rich/console.py:1165-1167), otherwise False (rich/console.py:1168), same as reference.diff:72-75.

ControlCode gains a Tuple[ControlType, str] member (rich/segment.py:59). The reference instead widens the second member to Union[int, str] (reference.diff:141-143). Both are valid typings for the same contract, so this is an accepted alternative.

No new imports are added in any touched source file. rich/console.py already imports Control at line 56, and rich/_windows_renderer.py already imports cast, Tuple and ControlType (line 1 and line 4 of that file).
rich/console.py depends on rich/control.py through the existing Control import; the win32 specifics stay in the renderer and LegacyWindowsTerm.
New enum member ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 at rich/segment.py:52; the existing maximum was 15, so there is no collision.
Formatter registered in CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT at rich/control.py:33 (ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE: lambda title: f"\x1b]0;{title}\x07"), matching reference.diff:95.
Legacy Windows dispatch added at rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56, calling term.set_title. LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title already exists in the base at rich/_win32_console.py:534.
No dependency, package or import is added by the patch. The only new code uses existing modules (rich.control, rich.segment, typing.Tuple/cast).

The Console method delegates to Control.title and is gated on is_terminal (rich/console.py:1165-1168), the same shape as the sibling methods show_cursor (base rich/console.py:1150) and set_alt_screen (base rich/console.py:1170).
Escape-sequence construction stays in rich/control.py, and Win32 calls stay behind the renderer, matching the reference's layering (reference.diff:72-73, 95, 34-36).

The feature uses the existing extension mechanisms: a ControlType member, the CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT table (rich/control.py:33), a Control classmethod (rich/control.py:151-161) and the legacy_windows_render elif chain (rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56). No parallel rendering path is created.
This matches how the existing controls such as CURSOR_MOVE_TO_COLUMN and ERASE_IN_LINE are wired (rich/_windows_renderer.py:39-53).
Console code calls only Control.title; it does not touch the Win32 API.
The renderer calls the existing LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title (rich/_windows_renderer.py:56, rich/_win32_console.py:534), which keeps the Win32 boundary intact.
The escape sequence is built only in control.py (rich/control.py:33).

tests/test_console.py:299-301 adds @pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="legacy Windows console has no title sequence"). The test then builds Console(..., legacy_windows=False) at tests/test_console.py:303-304.

The neighbouring test test_show_cursor (base tests/test_console.py:289-296) uses the same explicit legacy_windows=False pattern with no platform skip. The skip reason does not apply to a non-legacy console, so the new test is skipped on Windows without a reason and loses coverage there.

This is minor. It does not affect production code, and the rest of the conventions are followed: Args/Returns docstrings (rich/console.py:1155-1168), an Unreleased/Added changelog entry (CHANGELOG.md:9-11), the existing legacy_term_mock fixture (tests/test_windows_renderer.py:19-20,128-135), and the existing Segment/ControlType imports in tests/test_control.py.
criteria.deficiency: Unnecessary win32 skipif with an inaccurate reason in tests/test_console.py:299-301. Its sibling test_show_cursor (base tests/test_console.py:289-296) uses the same explicit legacy_windows=False setup without a skip. The reference instead uses an in-body `if console.legacy_windows: return` guard, which is the repo's established test pattern (base tests/test_console.py:872-898). Removing the decorator would match the sibling convention. This is minor and does not affect runtime behavior.

evidence: Behavior: Console.set_window_title writes the OSC 0 sequence "\x1b]0;{title}\x07" through the Control path (rich/control.py:33, rich/console.py:1166), and returns True only when the output is a terminal (rich/console.py:1165-1168). This matches reference.diff:72-75 and reference.diff:95.
Legacy Windows consoles forward the title to term.set_title (rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56), which matches reference.diff:34-36.

The new tests check this behavior: tests/test_console.py:299-309 (escape bytes and True return), tests/test_control.py:10-16 (segment contents), tests/test_windows_renderer.py:128-135 (set_title forwarding). Tests were not run, per the instructions.
Patch omits reference-only extras (the verbose docstring warnings, the __main__ demo in control.py, and the test_live.py churn). These are not required behavior, so their absence is not a failure.
